dialogues.speaker: Pain-Grocer
dialogues.text: So the rumors of your formidable strength and resilience are true! You are really tough! That was a good fight!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Huh? Are you sure you want to spar with me again? You're so patient!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Well, it's my honor then!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Why are you asking about Grandmaster Hanakado all of a sudden? You're trying to get some information out from me, aren't you?

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Well, I'll tell you what I know. He and I are just business partners anyway, so we're not particularly close.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Business partners? But you two are just kids!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: So what? I've supplied Tsukumomono Groceries dozens of times. Like the small trees and rocks I pulled out when catching Onikabuto...

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: The stuff was then made into bonsai trees and rock gardens, and they look pretty impressive when placed in the store! They're sold in limited quantities from time to time, and together with Aoi's promotion, it's pretty good business!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Aoi praised me and said that the goods I delivered are great, and could even be worth a third of many precious treasures!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Grandmaster Hanakado always buys them at high prices, saying that he'll use them to build courtyards and hills in his Onikabuto arena and make a camp for his beetles.

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: So, by helping you and Grandmaster Hanakado in beetle fighting, I'm also helping Aoi's and my own business venture.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, now Paimon understands where that name came from...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, it sounds like Grandmaster Hanakado comes from a very rich family... Could his parents be millionaires in disguise?

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: I don't know much about that. All I know is that every time he buys my goods, I'll earn enough Mora for a few days' worth of Sakura Shrimp Crackers!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sakura Shrimp Crackers? That's it? Seems like he isn't so rich after all...

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Huh? What do you mean? ...You must make a lot of Mora then!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Maybe I'll just hang out with you, and you can pay me to be your beetle-battler!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Then I'll get to beetle-fight with you every day!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Money... money isn't that important! Don't get so excited!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Besides... {NICKNAME} isn't a beetle fighting professional, so even if you come with us, you won't get too many work opportunities.

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: Is that so? Forget about it then! Anyway... After my bonsai and rock gardens open for sale, don't forget to pay me a visit and buy something!

response.speaker: Pain-Grocer
response.text: #See you next time, {NICKNAME} and Skycleaving White-Iron Lavender Melon! If you don't mind, come and have beetle fights with me again!
